correctness.rationale: The cyclic normal matrix is exactly 2(A²+B²)I+2AB(T+T⁻¹). Its periodized geometric inverse directly yields the signed sample rows and an exact total-variation norm for every N≥3 and 0<t<1/2. Opposing signs across adjacent rows give strict knot-only localization; constant reproduction gives the positivity defect. Hyperbolic differentiation gives strict odd-case monotonicity, and alternating midpoint equations give the rank boundary. The standalone exact-rational checker independently tests 33 matrices plus midpoint and knot endpoints, without mistaking finite tests for infinite proof.

originality.rationale: General stability of quadrature-defined spline projections was proved by Grigorieff–Sloan (1998), while Crouzeix–Thomée (1987) concerns continuous L² projection. The full periodic two-site signed row, all-N parity formula, exact Gauss constant, and midpoint singular/finiteness dichotomy are not statements or implications of those inspected general estimates. Existing continuous-measure periodic spline results concern a different right-hand-side functional even where the two-point Gauss rule gives an identical Gram matrix. Priority may remain in unindexed numerical-analysis literature.

value.rationale: Sharp norm and positivity loss across all uniform periodic grid sizes and all symmetric two-point quadrature locations is a natural and reusable stability invariant, not an arbitrary finite slice. It locates every extremizing evaluation point and reveals a parity-dependent singular limit: even grids blow up as sites coalesce, while odd grids remain bounded by N. The exact Gauss constant sqrt(3), independent of even grid size, quantifies a standard quadrature design. This is a structural full-parameter classification beyond general boundedness.
